report:
PASS applies only to the declared restricted A–D assignment. The supplied arguments do not determine the K3 lower mass or decide universal vanishing for nonzero real Chern class. The original problem remains INCONCLUSIVE on this evidence.

I independently checked the current clarified author proof, the earlier author version, the private concentration/radial proof, the complete original report, and all six independent notes. The independent support DAG is n1→n2; {n1,n2}→n3; n1→n4; n5 has only task geometry and elementary calculations; {n3,n4,n5}→n6. Prior verdicts, source-read declarations, hashes and computational outputs were not used as mathematical premises.

A is established in arbitrary dimension n≥2 without closedness of omega. A smooth positive complementary form can be normalized by its positive omega-degree. Pointwise domination B_delta≤M_delta omega proves finiteness of each supremum. Under the stated bounded-subsequence antecedent, kappa=1/(M+1) gives strictly positive pairing of omega−kappa B_delta_j with every unnormalized smooth strictly positive dd^c-closed complementary test. Lamari therefore supplies distributions satisfying omega+dd^c v_j≥kappa B_delta_j. No restriction to radial tests or singular-current fibers occurs.

The canonical compactness argument is valid. Choose inner coordinate balls of radius r and outer balls of radius 4r, with fixed nonnegative quadratic corrections rho making v_j+rho psh. If v_j(x)≥−E in an inner ball, the radius-2r ball centered at x contains that inner ball and lies in the outer chart. Submean and v_j≤0 bound the negative integral on the inner ball by a fixed multiple of E+sup rho. Positive-volume overlaps provide bounded-below points in successive charts. The connected finite overlap graph, with finitely many possible starting charts, gives a uniform global L1 bound. Smooth volume comparability also bounds every relatively compact portion of the outer charts. Local compactness consequently yields an L1 limit. Canonical convolution recovery makes the corrected representatives agree pointwise on overlaps. The limit is genuinely quasi-psh and nontrivial. The independent note additionally proves preservation of supremum zero by moving-center submean inequalities at maximizers; that argument is sound.

Full-variable smooth testing gives B_delta_j→chi[ζ=0]: changing ζ to delta_j times the integration variable cancels the density scaling, and the tangential coefficients of the test converge uniformly on the fixed compact support. Distributional differentiation and positivity preserve the limiting current inequality. This limit is generally nonclosed. Locally choosing dd^c rho≥omega instead produces the CLOSED positive currents S=dd^c(v+rho). Their smooth differences contribute O(r²) to normalized Lelong masses; coordinate invariance therefore makes their Lelong numbers agree on overlaps. The upperlevel at kappa glues to a closed analytic subset of dimension at most n−1, hence a proper subset. Domination of kappa[ζ=0] gives containment of the entire inner hypersurface. Its intersections with finitely many global irreducible components cover the connected inner polydisk. A finite union of proper analytic subsets cannot cover it, so one component contains an open portion and consequently the whole polydisk. Its dimension is n−1. Excluding every bounded subsequence establishes actual divergence of C_delta on hypersurface-free X.

B is established under precisely the entire-chart, multiplicity-one Cartier hypothesis. It gives the nowhere-zero holomorphic frame e=s_D/ζ. Modifying any global smooth metric by a cutoff times log|e|² makes |s_D|²=|ζ|² near every sufficiently small cutoff support. The actual global functions F_delta=log(|s_D|²+delta²) are smooth. Off D, their Hessians equal −[r/(r+delta²)]curv(h) plus the semipositive term [delta²r/(r+delta²)²]d log r∧d^c log r. Compactness bounds the curvature by K omega, uniformly in delta; continuity extends the lower bound across D. On the prescribed chart, dd^c F_delta=delta²/(|ζ|²+delta²)² sigma_ζ, which is at least sigma_ζ/(4delta²) on |ζ|≤delta. Consequently B_delta≤4||p||∞(dd^c F_delta+K omega) globally. Smooth dd^c Stokes against every normalized test gives C_delta≤4||p||∞K. The author's epsilon formulation is equally valid. Neither proof extends this bound to unrelated divisors or arbitrary branch intersections.

C is established exactly for the displayed family. The identities dg∧beta=0 and eta∧c=0 give d(g eta beta)=0. Also dd^c(a eta²)=a'' beta eta² because the a'c eta² term has excessive horizontal degree. The top form eta² beta is everywhere positive, so closure forces a''=0; periodicity forces constant a. The complementary matrix diag(g,g,2a) proves strict positivity exactly when a,g>0. Direct squaring verifies the positive root gamma=sqrt(a)eta+g beta/(2sqrt(a)); the cofactor relation also proves uniqueness. On each fiber d^c t=dθ/(2π), so fiber integration gives D=TA(a+gbar) and R=(3/2)TA sqrt(a)gbar. With b=gbar, the sharp inequality follows from (a+b)³−(27/4)ab²=(b−2a)²(b+a/4). Equality is exactly b=2a. The complete Fejer example has positive nonconstant coefficients, fixed mean and unbounded concentrated peaks, while its degree and root volume remain fixed. Its analytic formulas establish these assertions without relying on finite symbolic checks.

D correctly applies A to the task-stipulated divisor-free K3 total space and preserves the limitations. Divergent linear pairings do not establish determinant or positive-root-volume divergence. The independent diagonal-matrix example illustrates that missing implication and is expressly not a construction of global normalized tests. C supplies only its specified-family bound. No admissible mass-collapse sequence, exact all-potential K3 lower mass, or universal nonzero-class conclusion follows.

I opened and checked the relevant statements and printed arguments in [Lamari](https://www.numdam.org/article/AIF_1999__49_1_263_0.pdf) and [Demailly](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf). The indexed task passages below record the expressly permitted foundational statements; the primary passages corroborate their attribution. The disclosed imported scope is retained: no recursive certification of Siu III.8.4 or all inherited subharmonic foundations is claimed. Task-specific geometric hypotheses are excluded from the external-premise list.

The original report's 16 foundational premises reduce to the seven claims below: original indices {0,7}, {1,8,9,10}, {2,11}, {3,12}, {4,13}, {5,14}, and {6,15}, respectively. All 18 actual historical bindings were checked against the full matching statements, rather than their short quotations alone. Harmless corrections: coordinate invariance is III.7.2; III.8.5 is a corollary; and the historical component wording must say 'contains an open portion,' with the explicit finite-component justification supplied in the current proof. The displayed historical range labelled coordinate-invariance context actually contains Jensen–Lelong material, so it was not credited for that claim. The original report's prose also mentions a negative-index passage that is absent from its actual structured passages. These bookkeeping issues do not affect the independently established restricted argument.

passages.statement: On every compact complex n-fold, n≥2, there exists a smooth strictly positive real (n−1,n−1) form Θ satisfying dd^cΘ=0 (Lamari, Proposition 1.3).
passages.quote:
On a compact complex n-fold there exists a smooth strictly positive real
(n-1,n-1) form killed by dd^c.

passages.statement: Let X be a compact complex n-fold and b a smooth real (1,1) form. If ∫X b∧Θ≥0 for every smooth strictly positive real dd^c-closed (n−1,n−1) form Θ, there exists a real distribution q with b+dd^c q≥0. No d-closedness hypothesis on b is required (Lamari, Lemma 3.3).
passages.quote:
On a compact complex n-fold there exists a smooth strictly positive real
(n-1,n-1) form killed by dd^c. For any smooth real(1,1) form b, positivity
of its pairing with every smooth strictly positive dd^c-closed(n-1,n-1)
form implies the existence of a real distribution q with b+dd^c q>=0.
There is no d-closedness hypothesis on b.

passages.statement: On an open Ω⊂C^n, a real distribution with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable genuine plurisubharmonic representative; convolution with rescaled nonnegative smooth radial probability kernels decreases pointwise to that representative as the scale tends to zero (Demailly I.4.20, I.5.5, I.5.8).
passages.quote:
A distribution with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable
genuine psh representative; local radial convolution decreases to it.

passages.statement: On connected Ω⊂C^n, a genuine plurisubharmonic function not identically −∞ is locally integrable. On any open Ω⊂C^n, Psh(Ω)∩L¹_loc(Ω) is closed in L¹_loc(Ω), and every L¹_loc-bounded subset is relatively compact (Demailly I.4.17, I.5.9).
passages.quote:
Genuine psh functions not identically minus infinity are locally integrable,
and the cone Psh intersect L1_loc is closed with relatively compact bounded
subsets.

passages.statement: Geometric Lelong numbers of closed positive currents are coordinate invariant and unchanged by adding a smooth current when the resulting current is also positive and closed. The integration current of a smooth analytic hypersurface has geometric Lelong number one at each of its points (Demailly III.5.9, III.7.2).
passages.quote:
For a CLOSED positive current of bidimension(p,p) on a complex manifold,
its geometric Lelong upperlevel sets{x:nu(T,x)>=c},c>0, are analytic sets of
dimension at most p. Lelong numbers are coordinate invariant, are unchanged
by adding a smooth current, and nu([smooth hypersurface],x)=1 on its smooth
locus.

passages.statement: For a closed positive current T of bidimension (p,p) on a complex manifold, every upperlevel set {x:ν(T,x)≥c}, c>0, is analytic and has complex dimension at most p (Demailly III.8.5).
passages.quote:
For a CLOSED positive current of bidimension(p,p) on a complex manifold,
its geometric Lelong upperlevel sets{x:nu(T,x)>=c},c>0, are analytic sets of
dimension at most p.

passages.statement: An analytic set has a unique locally finite family of global irreducible components, each a closed irreducible analytic subset, whose union is the analytic set. If the analytic set is compact, this family is finite (Demailly II.5.3).
passages.quote:
An analytic set has a unique locally finite family of global irreducible
components, each a closed irreducible analytic subset, whose union is that
analytic set. On a compact space this family is finite.
